title: The Song of All Songs
subtitle: Song of Solomon 1:1-4
description: The Song of Solomon opens with the bride's passionate declaration of love. Explore the Puritan vision of marital love as a holy gift — a love better than wine, fragrant as poured-out ointment, and worthy of celebration.
memoryVerse: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine. — Song of Solomon 1:2
reflectionPrompt: Is there anything in your life more satisfying than the love you share with your spouse?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the gift of marital love and ask Him to renew your delight in one another.

title: Dark but Lovely
subtitle: Song of Solomon 1:5-8
description: The bride confesses her insecurity about her appearance, revealing the tender vulnerability that exists within every marriage. Learn how covenant love creates safety for honest self-disclosure.
memoryVerse: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem. — Song of Solomon 1:5
reflectionPrompt: Are there insecurities you have never fully shared with your spouse?
prayerFocus: Pray for healing in the tender, wounded places of your marriage.

title: Behold, Thou Art Fair
subtitle: Song of Solomon 1:9-17
description: The bridegroom responds to his bride's insecurity with lavish admiration. Discover the Puritan 'duty of commendation' — the life-giving practice of speaking specific praise to your spouse.
memoryVerse: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes. — Song of Solomon 1:15
reflectionPrompt: When was the last time you spoke words of genuine admiration to your spouse about who they are?
prayerFocus: Pray that God would give you eyes to see beauty in each other and mouths filled with praise.

title: The Rose of Sharon
subtitle: Song of Solomon 2:1-4
description: The beloved's love transforms the bride's self-image from darkened laborer to Rose of Sharon. Explore the banqueting house where love's banner is unfurled over the marriage covenant.
memoryVerse: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love. — Song of Solomon 2:4
reflectionPrompt: Is your home more like a banqueting house or a fast-food drive-through?
prayerFocus: Pray that your home would become a true banqueting house of abundance, delight, and celebration.

title: Stay Me with Flagons
subtitle: Song of Solomon 2:5-7
description: The bride is lovesick — overwhelmed by the intensity of love. Discover the Song's wisdom about love's rhythms, the beauty of patience, and the charge not to awaken love before its time.
memoryVerse: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please. — Song of Solomon 2:7
reflectionPrompt: Are you honoring each other's pace — physically, emotionally, spiritually?
prayerFocus: Pray for wisdom to honor the rhythms of your marriage and sensitivity to each other's needs.

title: The Voice of My Beloved
subtitle: Song of Solomon 2:8-13
description: The beloved leaps over mountains to reach his bride, inviting her to arise and come away — for winter is past and spring has come. A passage about renewal, pursuit, and the promise of new seasons.
memoryVerse: Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away. For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone. — Song of Solomon 2:10-11
reflectionPrompt: What season is your marriage in right now? What signs of spring might be emerging?
prayerFocus: Pray for renewal in your marriage and courage to answer the beloved's call to come away.

title: The Little Foxes
subtitle: Song of Solomon 2:14-17
description: Catch the little foxes that spoil the vines! This passage addresses the small habits and patterns that slowly destroy marriages — and the covenant declaration that stands against them all.
memoryVerse: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies. — Song of Solomon 2:16
reflectionPrompt: What little foxes can you identify in your marriage — small habits or attitudes that are slowly causing damage?
prayerFocus: Pray for the protection of your marriage vineyard and the grace to catch the foxes while they are still little.

title: By Night on My Bed
subtitle: Song of Solomon 3:1-5
description: The bride searches for her beloved through the dark city streets. A powerful passage about the ache of disconnection, the courage to pursue, and the determination never to let go.
memoryVerse: I held him, and would not let him go. — Song of Solomon 3:4
reflectionPrompt: When you feel disconnected from your spouse, do you tend to pursue or withdraw?
prayerFocus: Pray for the courage to pursue each other through seasons of distance and to hold on when you find each other.

title: The Day of His Espousals
subtitle: Song of Solomon 3:6-11
description: Solomon's grand wedding procession — a chariot of gold and silver, armed guards, and a heart paved with love. Remember your wedding day and the covenant that anchors your marriage.
memoryVerse: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals. — Song of Solomon 3:11
reflectionPrompt: What specific moments from your wedding day still move you? Share one with each other.
prayerFocus: Return to your wedding vows in prayer and ask God to guard your marriage with valiant warriors of truth and grace.

title: Thou Art All Fair
subtitle: Song of Solomon 4:1-7
description: The bridegroom's detailed, patient catalogue of his bride's beauty — from eyes to hair to lips to neck. A masterclass in attentive appreciation and the declaration: there is no spot in thee.
memoryVerse: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee. — Song of Solomon 4:7
reflectionPrompt: Take turns naming three specific things you find beautiful about each other.
prayerFocus: Pray for eyes to behold each other's beauty and mouths filled with specific, genuine praise.

title: Come with Me from Lebanon
subtitle: Song of Solomon 4:8-11
description: The bridegroom calls his bride away from the old life and into the new — an invitation to leave and cleave. Explore the Puritan wisdom on building a marriage that takes priority over all other bonds.
memoryVerse: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes. — Song of Solomon 4:9
reflectionPrompt: Is there anything from your past that still competes with your marriage for first place?
prayerFocus: Pray for the grace to leave fully and cleave completely to one another.

title: A Garden Enclosed
subtitle: Song of Solomon 4:12-16
description: The bride is a garden enclosed, a spring shut up, a fountain sealed — overflowing with spices and living water. Discover the sacred privacy of marriage and the abundance it produces.
memoryVerse: A garden enclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed. — Song of Solomon 4:12
reflectionPrompt: Is there any area where the wall of your marital privacy has been breached?
prayerFocus: Pray for the protection of your marriage's sacred privacy and the flourishing of everything within.

title: I Am Come into My Garden
subtitle: Song of Solomon 5:1
description: The consummation of marital love — and the remarkable voice of God Himself speaking blessing over the couple: 'Eat, O friends; drink abundantly, O beloved.' God celebrates your love.
memoryVerse: Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved. — Song of Solomon 5:1
reflectionPrompt: Do you carry any guilt or shame about the physical dimension of your marriage? How does God's blessing speak to that?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the gift of physical and emotional intimacy and ask Him to remove any shame that does not belong.

title: Guarding the Garden Together
subtitle: Song of Solomon 4:16-5:1 Review
description: A week-two summary gathering the riches of the bride's search, the wedding procession, the bridegroom's praise, the enclosed garden, and the divine blessing into a unified vision of marriage.
memoryVerse: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. — Song of Solomon 4:16
reflectionPrompt: Which teaching from this week has been most meaningful to your marriage?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the truths received and pray that they would be rooted deeply in your marriage.

title: I Opened to My Beloved, but He Was Gone
subtitle: Song of Solomon 5:2-8
description: The most painful passage in the Song — a missed connection, delayed response, and agonizing separation. A searching lesson about responsiveness and the cost of convenience in marriage.
memoryVerse: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone. — Song of Solomon 5:6
reflectionPrompt: Has there been a recent moment when one of you reached out and the other was too comfortable to respond?
prayerFocus: Pray for attentiveness and responsiveness — that you would never be too settled to open the door when your beloved knocks.

title: What Is Thy Beloved More Than Another?
subtitle: Song of Solomon 5:9-16
description: Asked to describe her beloved, the bride launches into a head-to-toe catalogue of his beauty, culminating in: 'He is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend.'
memoryVerse: Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem. — Song of Solomon 5:16
reflectionPrompt: Take turns answering: What makes your spouse different from anyone else? Be specific.
prayerFocus: Thank God for the specific qualities you see in your spouse and pray over each other by name.

title: Whither Is Thy Beloved Gone?
subtitle: Song of Solomon 6:1-3
description: In describing her beloved, the bride realizes where he has been all along — in the garden. Reunion comes through remembrance. 'I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine.'
memoryVerse: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies. — Song of Solomon 6:3
reflectionPrompt: How has your love matured from a focus on receiving to a focus on giving?
prayerFocus: Pray for the grace of mutual belonging — fully given, fully committed, fully each other's.

title: Thou Art Beautiful, O My Love
subtitle: Song of Solomon 6:4-10
description: After reconciliation, the bridegroom's praise is even more lavish than before — beautiful as Tirzah, terrible as an army with banners. Love tested and proven is love deepened.
memoryVerse: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners? — Song of Solomon 6:10
reflectionPrompt: After conflict, how quickly do you return to affirming each other?
prayerFocus: Pray for renewed wonder in your marriage — the ability to be astonished by each other.

title: The Dance of Mahanaim
subtitle: Song of Solomon 6:11-13
description: The bride returns to the garden to inspect its growth, and her soul leaps like a chariot. A passage about checking on your marriage's health and making room for spontaneous love.
memoryVerse: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. — Song of Solomon 6:13
reflectionPrompt: What growth do you see in your spouse that was not there when you first married?
prayerFocus: Thank God for growth and pray for the grace of spontaneous, overflowing love.

title: How Fair and How Pleasant
subtitle: Song of Solomon 7:1-9
description: The bridegroom's most lavish praise reaches its zenith — a complete, unreserved celebration of his bride's beauty. A passage about full-hearted admiration and intentional pursuit.
memoryVerse: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights! — Song of Solomon 7:6
reflectionPrompt: Is your admiration of your spouse selective or whole-person? What have you stopped noticing?
prayerFocus: Thank God for your spouse — body, mind, and soul — and pray for freedom to delight without reservation.

title: I Am My Beloved's
subtitle: Song of Solomon 7:10-13
description: The final declaration of belonging: 'I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.' An invitation to go forth into the field together, seeking new adventures and new fruit.
memoryVerse: I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me. — Song of Solomon 7:10
reflectionPrompt: Does your spouse know that your desire is toward them — not out of habit, but out of genuine longing?
prayerFocus: Pray for desire and adventure in your marriage — fresh longing and new experiences together.

title: O That Thou Wert as My Brother
subtitle: Song of Solomon 8:1-4
description: The bride longs for the freedom to express her love openly — a passage about the integration of private and public affection and the gift of giving your best to your beloved.
memoryVerse: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate. — Song of Solomon 8:2
reflectionPrompt: Does your spouse get the spiced wine — your best energy and attention — or the leftovers?
prayerFocus: Pray for a love that is unashamed, uncontained, and generous in every setting.

title: Set Me as a Seal upon Thine Heart
subtitle: Song of Solomon 8:5-7
description: The theological summit of the Song: love is strong as death, jealousy cruel as the grave, and the flame of love is the very flame of the Lord. Many waters cannot quench it.
memoryVerse: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death. — Song of Solomon 8:6
reflectionPrompt: What many waters have tried to quench the flame of your love — and how has your love survived?
prayerFocus: Pray Song of Solomon 8:6-7 over your marriage: ask God to set you as a seal upon each other's hearts.

title: Our Little Sister
subtitle: Song of Solomon 8:8-10
description: The Song turns outward to the next generation — preparing a younger woman for marriage, building walls of virtue, and the responsibility of mature love to mentor emerging love.
memoryVerse: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour. — Song of Solomon 8:10
reflectionPrompt: Is your marriage modeling something worth imitating for the younger people around you?
prayerFocus: Pray for the next generation — that they would be walls of virtue when the day of courtship comes.

title: Make Haste, My Beloved
subtitle: Song of Solomon 8:11-14
description: The Song's finale — the bride's vineyard, the bridegroom's longing to hear her voice, and the final cry: 'Make haste, my beloved.' Love ends not with satisfaction but with holy longing.
memoryVerse: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices. — Song of Solomon 8:14
reflectionPrompt: What has been the most meaningful lesson for your marriage from the Song of Solomon this month?
prayerFocus: Pray the final words of the Song over your lives and for the return of Christ, the ultimate Bridegroom.

title: Christ and the Song
subtitle: Song of Solomon Overview — Ephesians 5:25-27
description: The Puritan allegorical reading of the Song — how Christ's love for His church is the divine pattern behind every healthy marriage, and how the Gospel transforms the way couples love.
memoryVerse: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it. — Ephesians 5:25
reflectionPrompt: How does seeing your marriage as a picture of Christ and the church change your daily interactions?
prayerFocus: Pray that your marriage would increasingly mirror the love of Christ for His church.

title: The Song's Wisdom on Conflict
subtitle: Song of Solomon 5:2-6:3 Revisited
description: Five Puritan principles for navigating marital conflict: charitable interpretation, quick reconciliation, mutual humility, persistent pursuit, and restored delight.
memoryVerse: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine. — Song of Solomon 6:3
reflectionPrompt: Which of the five conflict principles do you most need right now?
prayerFocus: Pray for wisdom and humility to handle conflict well — quick to listen, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

title: The Song's Wisdom on Intimacy
subtitle: Song of Solomon Overview — Five Dimensions of Closeness
description: The Puritan vision of comprehensive marital intimacy: physical, emotional, spiritual, intellectual, and experiential — five dimensions woven into one garment of closeness.
memoryVerse: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. — Song of Solomon 8:6
reflectionPrompt: Of the five dimensions of intimacy, which is strongest and which is weakest in your marriage?
prayerFocus: Pray for intimacy in every dimension — physical, emotional, spiritual, intellectual, and experiential.

title: The Christian Directory on Marriage
subtitle: Richard Baxter's Counsel for Couples
description: Drawing from Richard Baxter's Christian Directory: the duties of delight, patience, communication, mutual sanctification, unity, and sexual faithfulness in marriage.
memoryVerse: Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering. — Colossians 3:12
reflectionPrompt: Which of Baxter's six duties speaks most urgently to your marriage?
prayerFocus: Pray through Baxter's six duties: delight, patience, communication, sanctification, unity, faithfulness.

title: Domestical Duties
subtitle: William Gouge's Vision for the Household
description: William Gouge's three bonds of marriage — covenant, companionship, and physical union — and his vision of marriage as a school where both partners grow in Christlikeness.
memoryVerse: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it. — Ephesians 5:25
reflectionPrompt: Of Gouge's three bonds — covenant, companionship, physical union — which needs the most attention?
prayerFocus: Pray over the three bonds and ask God to strengthen each one in your marriage.

title: A Good Wife Sent from the Lord
subtitle: Thomas Gataker's Marriage Sermons
description: Thomas Gataker's five marriage duties: gratitude, cherishing, companionship, kindness in speech, and perseverance. Marriage as 'the sweetest society of life' — a divine gift to be treasured.
memoryVerse: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the Lord. — Proverbs 18:22
reflectionPrompt: What is the single most important thing you want to carry forward from this month's study?
prayerFocus: Pray a prayer of gratitude for the Song of Solomon's vision of love and the spouse who sits beside you.
